nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) implemented using PCNtoolkit (version 0.27). The HBR approach accommodates signal and noise variance in data from multiple sites by estimating different but connected mean and variance components through shared prior distributions across sites. A separate HBR model was estimated for each ROI and each receptor system (443 ROIs x 6 molecular systems).
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: We implemented our normative models using the PCNtoolkit (version 0.27). We chose to utilise a hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) approach which can accommodate signal and noise variance in data from multiple sites by estimating different but connected mean and variance components through shared prior distributions across sites.

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Molecular-enriched functional connectivity (FC) values for each ROI and receptor system.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: a separate model is /uniFB01 t for each region of the brain within each of the different molecular-enriched networks derived from our REACT and parcellation pipeline), using the age and sex of participants to build a predictive model of molecular-enriched FC values.

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age and sex were used as fixed effects. Site (UCLA, Cambridge) was used as a random effect in the hierarchical Bayesian regression model. The model was trained on 70% of healthy control data from both CamCAN and UCLA datasets (train: CamCAN=346, UCLA=78; test: CamCAN=150, UCLA=33).
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: Specifically, we used site (UCLA, Cambridge) as a random effect as well as age and sex as fixed effects, resulting in normative regional molecular-enriched FC variance and uncertainty.
